chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the testimony of the children allowed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, regarding the killing, he would be taken with the first of his speech, and he would not be taken from the second one from it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the testimony of children in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle of 'sahih al-shahadah' (valid testimony) for children in homicide cases, emphasizing the legal doctrine of 'qabul al-kalam al-awwal' (acceptance of the first statement). It highlights the Shia scholarly approach to evidentiary reliability, prioritizing the initial, uncorrupted declaration over later potential inconsistencies or confusion. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic law to accommodate varying levels of cognitive maturity in critical legal proceedings.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is the testimony of the children allowed?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, regarding the killing, he would be taken with the first of his speech, and he would not be taken from the second one from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz who has narrated the following:

“I once asked Tsma’il ibn Ja’far, ’When it is permissible for a boy to testify?’ He said, ’It is permissible when he becomes ten years old.’ I then asked, ‘Can he issue a command?’ He said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, went to bed with ‘A’ishah when she was ten years old and it is not permissible to go to bed with a girl unless she is a woman (‘A’ishah was not underage). When a boy becomes ten years old his commanding is permissible and his testimony is admissible.’” (They have mentioned his words perhaps to show his invalid analogizing effort)
